# Copper Scroll Column 3 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Copper Scroll Column 3 (treasure locations 9-12) where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 3:1 — plastered cistern phrasing

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the plastered cistern of the Queen" |
| LOGOS | "the plastered cistern belonging to the Queen" |
| PNEUMA | "the lime-plastered water cistern of the Queen" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET's concise "the plastered cistern of the Queen." PNEUMA's "lime-plastered water cistern" over-specifies; LOGOS's "belonging to" is unnecessarily wordy.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 3:3 — bottom/floor

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "from the bottom" — literal |
| LOGOS | "from the bottom" — same |
| PNEUMA | "from the floor" — variant |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "from the bottom" per EMET/LOGOS consensus.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 3:5 — entrance/mouth + waterfall placement

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "At the entrance of the waterfall of Beth Sham" |
| LOGOS | "At the mouth of the waterfall at Beth Sham" |
| PNEUMA | "At the waterfall entrance near Beth Sham" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS's "mouth of the waterfall" — pi in Hebrew literally means "mouth." "At Beth Sham" preferred over "of Beth Sham" for the locative.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 3:9 — opposite/facing/across from

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "opposite the east gate" |
| LOGOS | "facing the eastern gate" |
| PNEUMA | "across from the eastern gate" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "opposite the eastern gate" — EMET's "opposite" with LOGOS's "eastern" (adjective form is more natural than noun modifier).

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS blend.

---

## 3:13-14 — underground passage/subterranean passage/underground corridor + storehouse/treasury

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "underground passage" and "storehouse" |
| LOGOS | "subterranean passage" and "storehouse" |
| PNEUMA | "underground corridor" and "treasury" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "underground passage" (EMET) and "storehouse" (EMET/LOGOS). "Corridor" implies a specific architectural form; "treasury" over-interprets otsar which means storehouse.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 3:16 — eight and a half / eight and one-half

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "eight and a half" |
| LOGOS | "eight and one-half" — formal |
| PNEUMA | "eight and a half" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "eight and a half" per EMET/PNEUMA. More natural English; LOGOS's "one-half" is overly formal.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/PNEUMA.

---

*Total disagreements in Column 3: 6*
